main_text.p: [?] Syr. Ultor, Vindex, 1. ad Thessalon. 4.6. ad Roman. 13.4.
[?] Syr. Ultio, Vindicta, Luc.18.7.8.& 21.22.2. ad Thess.1.8.2. ad Cor.7.11.

תְּבַר Chald. Syriac. Frangere, confringere, diffringere, effringere, perfringere, perrumpere, disrumpere: & metaphoricè, Frangi animo, terreri, consternari. Pahel תְּבַר Idem. Ithpehal אִתְבַּר, Ithpahel אִתְבַּר Confractus, consternatus fuit. Syriac. Futur. [?] Non confringetur in eo, Johan.19.36. Ab Hebraeo שבר, mutato pro more ש in ת. At Exo.22.8. in Jonath. pro דְּאִתְבִּיר legendum est דְּאִתְבִּיר Quod amissum est, per ד ex אבר.
תְּבִירָא Ch. Fractum, confractum, discerptum: & substantivè Fractio, confractio, contritio, Psal.89.41. Esth.6.1. Thren.1.15. Pl.Syr. [?] Contriti corde, Luc.4.18.19.
תְּבָרָא, תְּבָר, תַּבְרָא Ch. Fractura, fractio, confractio, contritio. Plur. תִּבְרִין.
מִתְבְּרִין Chaldaicè, Fluctus, Psalm.42.8. Hebraicè, מִשְׁבָּרִים.
תְּנָא Chald. Corona, diadema, Esth.2.17.19. Plur. constr.

page.notes: Many Hebrew and Syriac words are small and smudged; their vowel points and letters are uncertain and marked [?]. The Syriac entries at the top could not be read letter by letter and are only approximated in Hebrew-style letters, so treat those marked [?] with caution. Entries are set as separate paragraphs, each starting with its Hebrew or Syriac word.
